quests.name: The Tyrian Commission
quests.description: Nikias, a merchant of Athens, asks you to deliver Attic pottery to Tyre and return with Tyrian purple dye.

objectives.description: Purchase Tyrian purple dye at Tyre
Return with Tyrian purple to Piraeus

rewards.title: The Tyrian Commission Complete
rewards.text: Nikias is pleased with the Tyrian purple. The rich dye, extracted from murex sea snails by Phoenician artisans, will fetch a handsome price at the Athenian agora.

quests.historicalNote: Tyrian purple (porphyra) was the most prized dye in the ancient Mediterranean, worth more than gold by weight. Produced from the mucus of Bolinus brandaris sea snails, it took 10,000 snails to produce 1 gram of dye. Athens exported fine pottery (especially red-figure and black-figure ware) across the Mediterranean, making pottery-for-dye a historically plausible trade.

quests.name: The Grain of the Nile
quests.description: Taharqa, grain factor of Memphis, asks you to deliver Egyptian grain to Athens where it commands high prices.

rewards.title: The Grain of the Nile Complete
rewards.text: Taharqa's Egyptian grain has reached Athens. The Athenians depend on imported grain -- their rocky Attic soil produces olives and grapes but not enough wheat to feed the city. Egypt, blessed by the annual Nile flood, is the breadbasket of the Mediterranean.

quests.historicalNote: Egypt was the primary grain supplier to the ancient Mediterranean world. The annual Nile flood (akhet) deposited rich black silt across the floodplain, enabling massive agricultural surpluses. Athens, with its poor soil for grain cultivation, imported heavily from Egypt and the Black Sea region. Herodotus Book II extensively documents Egyptian agriculture and trade customs.

quests.name: The Pillars of Melqart
quests.description: Elissa of Carthage asks you to sail beyond the Pillars of Melqart to Gadir and bring back Iberian wine.

objectives.description: Sail to Gadir beyond the Pillars

rewards.title: The Pillars of Melqart Complete
rewards.text: The Iberian wine has reached Carthage. Elissa is pleased. The voyage beyond the Pillars of Melqart taught me that the Phoenician trade network extends far beyond the Inner Sea, reaching the Atlantic coast of Iberia.

quests.historicalNote: The Pillars of Melqart (Greek: Pillars of Heracles, modern: Strait of Gibraltar) marked the boundary between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic. Gadir (modern Cadiz) was the oldest Phoenician colony in the west, founded c. 1100 BCE. Carthage controlled western Mediterranean trade routes. Maria Eugenia Aubet's 'The Phoenicians and the West' documents this extensive trade network.

quests.name: Roman Tribute
quests.description: Hanno, customs collector at Ostia, asks you to bring fine Athenian olive oil to the growing city of Rome.

rewards.title: Roman Tribute Complete
rewards.text: The Athenian olive oil has reached Rome. Hanno assures me the magistrates will remember this service. Rome is still a young republic, but her ambition is clear -- she will need many traders in the years to come.

quests.historicalNote: In 540-530 BCE, Rome had recently transitioned from monarchy to republic (traditional date: 509 BCE). Ostia served as Rome's port. Olive oil was essential for Roman daily life -- cooking, lighting, bathing, and religious rituals. Athens was renowned for producing the finest olive oil, pressed from the sacred olive trees of Athena. Livy and Braudel document early Roman trade patterns.

quests.name: The Cedar of Lebanon
quests.description: Aziru, a Phoenician merchant of Tyre, asks you to bring wine from Byblos for a ship-launching celebration.

objectives.description: Visit the ancient city of Byblos

rewards.title: The Cedar of Lebanon Complete
rewards.text: The wine from Byblos has reached Tyre. Aziru's shipwrights will celebrate the launching of their newest vessel. The Phoenician coast -- Tyre, Sidon, Byblos -- is the cradle of Mediterranean seamanship.

quests.historicalNote: Byblos (modern Jbeil, Lebanon) is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It was the center of the cedar trade -- Lebanese cedar was essential for shipbuilding, construction, and Egyptian coffin-making. The very word 'Bible' derives from Byblos, as it was the primary source of papyrus imported from Egypt. Boardman's 'The Greeks Overseas' documents Phoenician trade along the Levantine coast.

quests.name: The Merchant's Odyssey
quests.description: Complete all commissions across the Mediterranean to prove yourself as a master merchant captain.

objectives.description: Complete the Grain of the Nile

rewards.title: The Merchant's Odyssey Complete
rewards.text: I have sailed the length of the Mediterranean, from the Pillars of Melqart to the ports of the Levant. I have traded with Phoenicians, Egyptians, Romans, and Carthaginians. The sea has been my teacher and the ports my classroom. I am a master merchant of Mare Nostrum.

quests.historicalNote: A merchant captain in the 6th century BCE who had traded across the entire Mediterranean would have been among the most worldly and educated people alive. Through trade, ancient merchants were the primary vectors for cultural exchange -- spreading the Phoenician alphabet, Greek philosophy, Egyptian astronomy, and technological innovations across the known world.
